pathway.title: Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage depends on which EBITDA the committee accepts, and the defensible range is 4.09x to 5.48x, not the issuer's 3.59x. Net debt of USD 2,656 million is 5.48x unadjusted EBITDA of USD 485 million and 3.59x the issuer's adjusted EBITDA of USD 740 million; removing only the Revo charges of USD 164 million gives 4.09x, because the other add-backs of USD 91 million, mainly stock-based compensation and development advance note amortization, recur every year. The creditor consequence is that the headline 3.59x understates the burden, and the reported first-lien covenant ratio of 2.0x against a 5.0x maximum, which cannot be rebuilt without the credit agreement, does not offset that. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1

Near-term refinancing risk is low, but rate and refinancing risks cluster in 2027 and 2028. Liquidity of USD 988 million covers the USD 542 million of debt due within 24 months 1.82x, and only USD 23 million falls due within a year, with the USD 500 million notes due in August 2028 the first large maturity. Interest rate swaps of USD 475 million expire in the fourth quarter of 2027 and USD 950 million in the second and third quarters of 2028, and they hedge over 95% of the term loan B; once they lapse, each 100 bp on USD 1,500 million would cost USD 15.00 million a year, or 4.55% of last-twelve-months free cash flow. The creditor consequence is that the 2028 notes and the swap roll-off fall in the same window, so a refinancing plan and a hedging decision are due together. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C8

Cash conversion is adequate, but shareholder returns, not operations, decide whether leverage falls. Free cash flow was USD 330 million over the last twelve months, 44.59% of adjusted EBITDA, while dividends and repurchases were USD 368 million, or 111.52% of free cash flow, and 122.43% in FY2025 and 151.55% in the nine months to 2026-09-30. Had the USD 100 million by which returns exceeded free cash flow in those nine months been kept, net leverage would be 0.21x lower on unadjusted EBITDA and 0.14x lower on adjusted. The creditor consequence is that the board can restore deleveraging quickly by cutting buybacks, and has not yet done so. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4

Revenue is recurring, but the fee base is not growing in dollars: rooms grow and royalty income does not. System rooms grew 2.57% year on year to 2026-09-30, or 3.74% excluding Revo, yet royalties and franchise fees fell 2.62% in nine months 2026 to USD 409 million from USD 420 million, because Revo fees are deferred, all net room growth came from international rooms that earned a 2.6% royalty rate in the third quarter against 4.7% in the United States, and global RevPAR is flat over the nine months. Net revenue growth of USD 17 million came from ancillary income of USD 24 million, mainly the co-branded credit card programme, and USD 9 million of management and other fees, mainly from two owned hotels, less USD 11 million of lower royalties and franchise fees and USD 5 million of lower marketing revenue. About USD 8 million of the USD 22 million rise in adjusted EBITDA is a swing in the marketing, reservation and loyalty margin from a loss of USD 1 million to a surplus of USD 7 million, which the issuer links to the absence of the 2025 franchisee conference and to timing of spend. The creditor consequence is that recent earnings growth leans on partner fees and a better marketing margin rather than on the core fee base. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5; calculation C6

Franchisee credit is the main source of loss outside the debt figure. The Revo insolvency wrote off USD 160 million of USD 197 million of book value, while development advance notes of USD 383 million equal 80.63% of stockholders' equity and the issuer guarantees a share of some franchisee construction loans in an amount it does not state. A second failure of Revo's size would cut unadjusted EBITDA by USD 160 million and lift unadjusted net leverage to 8.17x, although the adjusted figure would stay at 3.59x because the charge is added back. The creditor consequence is that growth funded by advances turns franchisee failures into balance-sheet losses, and the add-back that hides them is the one a committee should test first. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7; calculation C9

Financial policy is the weakest dimension and the one creditors can least control. Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk Medium: no controlling holder is disclosed, so the board alone chooses returns, it added USD 400 million of repurchase capacity in September 2026, and finance leadership changed in 2026. The issuer states ratings of Ba1 from Moody's and BB+ from S&P and Fitch, which this analysis does not rely on or replace. The creditor consequence is that policy can change faster than the credit agreement protects against, and the restricted-payment baskets were not supplied. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40

runs.text: A recurring fee stream across a widely spread franchisee base is the main strength. Agreements run 10 to 20 years, more than six thousand franchisees pay royalties, none exceeds 2% of hotels, and free cash flow of USD 330 million over the last twelve months was 44.59% of adjusted EBITDA after development advances. This supports debt service through a slow year. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4

Liquidity and the maturity ladder give time. Liquidity of USD 988 million is 1.82x the USD 542 million due within 24 months, so a fall in fee income would reach leverage long before it reached liquidity. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C3

A small capital need keeps margins high. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 51.18% over the last twelve months and capital expenditure 3.22% of FY2025 revenue, so little of each dollar of fees is needed to maintain the system. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; calculation C10

Discretionary distributions are a lever. Repurchases of USD 239 million over the last twelve months can be cut without touching operations, which would let net debt fall. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4

Leverage is high on unadjusted EBITDA and has not fallen. Net leverage is 5.48x, 4.09x before the Revo charges and 3.59x on the issuer's adjusted measure, up from 4.17x at the end of FY2024 on unadjusted EBITDA. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1

Shareholder returns exceed free cash flow and net borrowing funds the gap. Returns were 111.52% of free cash flow over the last twelve months and 151.55% in nine months 2026, and net debt rose USD 160 million in nine months 2026. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4

Franchisee credit exposure has already cost USD 160 million. Development advance notes of USD 383 million equal 80.63% of equity, the collateral recovered so far from Revo was USD 23 million of hotel net assets, and the amount of franchisee loans the issuer guarantees is not stated. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9

The fee base is not growing in dollars. Royalties and franchise fees fell 2.62% in nine months 2026 while rooms grew 2.57%, and growth came from partner fees and two owned hotels. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C5

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The only new debt issue in the period is the February 2026 sale of USD 650 million of senior unsecured notes due 2033, with net proceeds of USD 642 million, a first call date of 2029-03-01 and semi-annual interest from 2026-09-01. The proceeds repaid revolver borrowings and term loan A, which removed the 2027 term loan maturity and left the August 2028 notes as the next large maturity, and added fixed interest of about USD 36.56 million a year. Wyndham also assumed USD 15 million of mortgages on the two European hotels it took by enforcing collateral against Revo in the first quarter of 2026. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C13

In October 2025 the issuer amended and extended its revolving credit facility, raising capacity to USD 1.0 billion, extending maturity to 2030 and cutting borrowing costs by 35 bp. No pending acquisition, disposal or new financing was described in the sources read, and the issuer states that it expects to fund all cash needs from cash on hand, operations and the revolver. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 61

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Subsequent events by date, kept out of period figures: Revo Hospitality Group had filed for insolvency by the time the FY2025 statements were prepared, and the January 2026 filing is described in the annual report signed 2026-02-19. In February 2026 the issuer sold USD 650 million of 5.625% senior unsecured notes (the supplemental indenture is dated 2026-02-27) and used the proceeds to repay the revolver and term loan A. In February 2026 the board raised the quarterly dividend to USD 0.43 per share. In the first quarter of 2026 the issuer enforced its Revo collateral and took two hotels. In September 2026 the board added USD 400 million to the repurchase authorisation. The newest source is signed 2026-10-22 and states no later event.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net leverage on unadjusted EBITDA rose from 4.17x at FY2024 to 5.38x at FY2025 and 5.48x on the last twelve months to 2026-09-30, while net leverage on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA moved from 3.40x to 3.48x and 3.59x. The gap between the two is the issuer's add-backs, USD 254 million in FY2025 and USD 255 million on the last twelve months, mostly stock-based compensation, development advance note amortization and the Revo charges. FY2025 deteriorated because Revo charges of USD 160 million cut unadjusted EBITDA while net debt rose USD 136 million; since then net debt has risen another USD 160 million as cash returned to shareholders exceeded free cash flow, and unadjusted net leverage has stayed between 5.32x and 5.51x at the three 2026 quarter ends as last-twelve-months unadjusted EBITDA recovered to USD 485 million. The creditor consequence is that leverage on unadjusted EBITDA stepped up in FY2025 and has not come back down, while the adjusted figure looks stable, so the add-backs carry the credit case.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Unadjusted EBITDA covered cash interest 4.49x in FY2024, 3.27x in FY2025 and 4.66x on the last twelve months, but the latest figure is flattered: cash interest paid fell to USD 104 million on the last twelve months from USD 142 million in FY2025 while net interest expense rose, and on net interest expense of USD 144 million the cover is 3.37x. The filings do not say why cash paid fell, so the improvement in cover is not a reliable signal of lower interest cost. The new 5.625% notes add about USD 36.56 million of fixed interest a year in place of floating-rate borrowings, which fixes part of the interest bill.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow after capital expenditure was USD 241 million in FY2024, USD 321 million in FY2025 and USD 194 million in nine months 2026, while dividends and repurchases were USD 432 million, USD 393 million and USD 294 million, which is 179.25%, 122.43% and 151.55% of free cash flow. Net borrowing of USD 296 million, USD 93 million and USD 160 million funded the difference. Operating cash flow is also after net payments of development advance notes of USD 75 million in nine months 2026; the notes, USD 383 million on the balance sheet at 2026-09-30 against USD 343 million at FY2025, are forgiven over the franchise term (USD 26 million in nine months) rather than repaid, so that cash is recovered only through fee income and is lost if the franchisee fails, as at Revo. The creditor consequence is that distributions are discretionary and can be cut, which is the main lever protecting leverage.

fields.value: Liquidity was USD 988 million at 2026-09-30, made up of USD 71 million of cash and USD 917 million undrawn on the USD 1,000 million revolver, against USD 840 million at FY2025 and USD 765 million at FY2024. The February 2026 notes replaced the term loan A due 2027 and revolver borrowings with debt due in 2033, so the next large maturity is the August 2028 notes (carrying USD 498 million) and then term loan B in May 2030 (carrying USD 1,491 million), with the revolver due in October 2030. Only USD 23 million falls due in the next twelve months and no committed facility expires within twelve months, and the issuer expects to fund all cash needs from cash on hand, operations and the revolver. The creditor consequence is that refinancing risk is low until 2028, and the revolver is the main source of cover if franchise fees weaken.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Deferred revenues of USD 354 million at 2026-09-30 (USD 135 million current and USD 219 million non-current) equal the remaining performance obligations the issuer reports, and stood at USD 354 million at FY2025 and USD 290 million at FY2024. This is cash franchisees and card partners paid in advance for brand, loyalty and fee services, and it funded part of operations at no interest; it grew USD 64 million in FY2025 and was flat in 2026. If new franchise signings or loyalty redemption patterns weakened, the float would stop growing and then reverse, and the issuer would owe the services without new cash. The creditor consequence is that part of reported operating cash flow is prepayment, not recurring earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside the debt figure are small beside USD 2,727 million of carrying debt. At FY2025 future interest on the debt was about USD 515 million (USD 141 million within twelve months) and purchase commitments for marketing and technology services were USD 168 million (USD 79 million within twelve months), both outside debt; operating lease liabilities are USD 3 million in current accrued expenses and there are no finance leases. The issuer also carries a one-third share of its former parent's contingent liabilities and related credit support, and about 80 pending litigation matters at 2026-09-30 for which it holds an accrual of USD 2 million and estimates no range; both are contingent and outside debt. No pension, retiree medical, factoring, supply-chain finance or consent-decree item was found in any of the five extracts. The creditor consequence is that the claims ranking alongside debt are minor, while the litigation count and the former parent's liabilities are unquantified tail risks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit facilities carry one financial maintenance covenant, a maximum first-lien leverage ratio of 5.0 times tested quarterly, and the sources state no step-down. The issuer reports 2.0 times at each 2026 quarter end, 2.8 times at FY2025 and 2.7 times at FY2024, and says it expects to stay in compliance. That ratio counts only first-lien debt net of unrestricted cash over the credit agreement's own EBITDA, so it is not the total leverage computed here: first-lien carrying debt of USD 1,574 million is 3.25x unadjusted EBITDA before netting cash, which indicates that the issuer's 2.0 times rests on a covenant EBITDA closer to its adjusted measure than to unadjusted EBITDA; the definition itself is not established. The creditor consequence is that the reported covenant position looks distant from the limit, but it cannot be tested because the credit agreement was not supplied, and no headroom is calculated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revo, a large European franchisee, filed for insolvency, and the issuer recorded charges of USD 160 million in FY2025: USD 86 million as impairment and USD 74 million within operating expenses. The same event appears as an impairment of USD 86 million in the cash flow statement beside a provision for doubtful accounts and loan losses of USD 87 million, against USD 4 million a year earlier (the filing does not say how much of the provision is Revo), as a reduction of USD 160 million in the carrying value of the related assets, and as add-backs of USD 86 million and USD 74 million in Adjusted EBITDA. In 2026 the issuer enforced its collateral, took two hotels with net assets of about USD 23 million and holds about USD 19 million of restricted cash whose release needs court approval. The creditor consequence is that the fee stream and receivables from that franchisee are lost or deferred, and the recovery from the collateral is small against the charge.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the issuer's margin and cash conversion: adjusted EBITDA margin has stayed near 50%, free cash flow was about 45% of adjusted EBITDA in FY2025 and on the last twelve months, liquidity has risen and leverage on the issuer's definition is moderate. That view would win if the Revo charges prove one-off, unadjusted EBITDA recovers toward the adjusted measure and the board holds distributions at or below free cash flow. The main data risks are that unadjusted EBITDA is calculated rather than stated, the covenant ratio cannot be rebuilt without the credit agreement, the cash interest figure is lumpy and operating statistics changed basis in 2025; each is logged in the definition conflict register and the gap lines.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA, so EBITDA (Reported) in every period is calculated as operating income plus depreciation and amortization; it restricts any comparison with an EBITDA the issuer defines differently, and the action that would close it is the issuer's own unadjusted figure or the credit agreement definition. Severity Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The first-lien leverage ratio the issuer reports (2.0 times in each 2026 quarter, 2.8 times for FY2025 and 2.7 times for FY2024, called annualized in the annual reports) cannot be rebuilt because the credit agreement definitions of first-lien debt and EBITDA were not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculated; supplying the credit agreement would close it. Severity Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash interest paid fell to USD 74 million in nine months 2026 from USD 112 million a year earlier while net interest expense rose, and the filings do not explain it, so the last-twelve-months cover of 4.66 times is flattered; the interest payment schedule would close it. Severity Medium.

fields.name: Quote

Severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Lines that a report does not print at all are not supplied for that report: Cost reimbursements, Impairment and Early extinguishment of debt in every interim income statement; in the cash flow statements Impairment, Loss on early extinguishment of debt, the gross Payments and Proceeds of development advance notes, Loan advances, Loan repayments and Finance lease payments in the interim reports, the net Payments of development advance notes and Loan advances, net in the annual reports, the financing Other, net in Q1 and H1, and the FX effect in Q1 2025 and Q1 2026; this restricts only comparisons of those lines across periods. Severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2025 quarterly reports were not supplied, so every Q1 to Q3, H1 and 9M 2025 figure comes from the comparative columns of the 2026 reports as the issuer presents them there; this restricts any check against the originally published 2025 quarters. Severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Term loan B principal is stated only as USD 1.5 billion, and the face amount of the mortgages is stated only as USD 15 million when assumed, so contractual principal by tranche is not exact; the gross principal is about USD 2,747 million against carrying value of USD 2,727 million, and the credit agreement would close it. Severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The annual amortisation of term loan B is 0.25% of the initial principal each quarter, but the initial principal is not stated, so scheduled annual amortisation in dollars is not supplied. Severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Interest income is stated only for the annual periods (USD 8 million in FY2025 and USD 5 million in FY2024) and not in the quarterly reports, so total interest expense is not separated from net interest expense for 2026. Severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cost of goods sold and gross profit are not presented because the issuer reports expenses by nature, and capital expenditure is not split into maintenance and growth; maintenance capital expenditure is therefore not supplied. Severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash flow statements are cumulative within the year, so discrete second and third quarter cash flows for 2026 and 2025 are not constructed; they would be differences of the half-year and nine-month figures. Severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Restricted cash of about USD 19 million at 2026-09-30 tied to the Revo collateral sits in other non-current assets and is not netted in net debt; its release needs court approval over months to years. Severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Letters of credit under the revolver are not printed in the debt tables, which deduct borrowings only, so undrawn availability of USD 917 million at 2026-09-30 may be overstated if any are outstanding; the credit agreement or a later filing would close it. Severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The sum of Q1 and Q2 2025 depreciation and amortization is 30 against 31 for the half year because the issuer rounds each period; both are kept as printed. Severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance fact base for Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, Inc. (wh-1722684), as of 2026-11-18, under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business model, franchise system, revenue mix, ownership and control, management, governance, capital allocation and the Revo franchisee insolvency, from the FY2024 and FY2025 annual reports and the Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 quarterly reports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Wyndham has no disclosed controlling holder and a diversified franchisee base, so creditor risk lies in management choices: shareholder returns have exceeded free cash flow, finance leadership turned over in 2026, and the large franchisee Revo became insolvent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Dividends and buybacks were 148.28% of free cash flow from 2023 to 2025 and 151.55% in the nine months to 2026-09-30, with net borrowing filling the gap, and the board added USD 400 million of repurchase capacity in September 2026. The Revo failure cost USD 160 million, 81.22% of the USD 197 million book exposure, and the former parent, Travel + Leisure, supplies licence fees equal to 7.07% of FY2025 net revenues. Sponsor and governance risk is Medium: no sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed that could extract value, but board composition, the size of the restricted-payment baskets and the notes' change-of-control terms were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 121; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C10; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The franchise system is diversified and fee-based, but the diversification is not complete. More than six thousand franchisees pay the fees, none is above 2% of hotels on the issuer's count, and the United States supplies 77% of royalty contribution, so no single owner decides the cash flow. The Revo insolvency shows the limit: the rooms implied for Revo were 2.60% of system rooms at 2025-09-30, above the 2% the issuer cites by hotel count, and the two measures are not comparable. The creditor consequence is that fee income is spread widely, yet one regional operator was large enough to cost USD 160 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C3; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported revenue overstates the fee base, because 39.33% of FY2025 net revenues is marketing, reservation and loyalty income that the issuer is generally obliged to spend for the system and that cost USD 3 million more than it raised that year. The profit-bearing streams are royalties and franchise fees at 37.86%, licence and other fees at 8.82% and partnership fees at 6.72%, together 53.39%, and the royalty rate is not rising: 4.0% globally and 4.7% in the United States in Q3 2026, against 4.0% and 4.8% a year earlier. The creditor consequence is that debt service rests on a narrower income base than the revenue line suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The former parent is a material related-party dependency. Travel + Leisure paid licence fees of USD 101 million in FY2025, 7.07% of net revenues and 12.22% above 2023, and two Wyndham directors sit on its board. Wyndham also carries one-third of the former parent's pre-spin contingent liabilities and guarantees of USD 127 million, with a fair value of USD 61 million, given on the former parent's sale of its European vacation rentals business, of which the former parent bears two-thirds of any loss, with a USD 41 million receivable from it. The creditor consequence is that weaker timeshare sales would cut fee income with no change in Wyndham's own hotels, and the contingent claims depend on the former parent paying its share; the quarterly reports repeat only the separation guarantee, so the current status of the credit support is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns are the clearest creditor-adverse behaviour, because they exceeded free cash flow in every period reviewed and were largely funded by net borrowing. Dividends and repurchases were 150.74% of free cash flow in 2023, 179.25% in 2024, 122.43% in 2025 and 151.55% in the nine months to 2026-09-30, a cumulative USD 1,336 million against USD 901 million of free cash flow over 2023 to 2025, with net borrowing of USD 522 million. Stockholders' equity fell 57.02% from USD 1,089 million at 2021 year-end to USD 468 million at 2025 year-end while total debt rose 22.84%, and in September 2026 the board added USD 400 million of repurchase capacity when USD 118.33 million remained at the end of August. The creditor consequence is that leverage is a board choice with no controlling holder to impose discipline, and the only restraint is the board's own policy and the restricted-payment covenant in the credit facilities, whose basket sizes were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 82; 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Revo insolvency shows that franchisee financing is a real credit exposure and that recoveries are slow. Revo carried USD 197 million of book value, of which USD 160 million, or 81.22%, was written off in FY2025, equal to 22.28% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA. In 2026 collateral enforcement took two European hotels with net assets of USD 23 million, equal to the loans and development advance notes they replaced, and about USD 19 million of restricted cash awaits court approval over months to years; Revo revenue is removed from the 2026 outlook and Revo rooms are excluded from the issuer's growth metrics. Wyndham keeps funding franchisees, with USD 105 million of development advance notes net of repayments in 2025 and about USD 110 million planned for 2026, and the notes stood at USD 383 million at 2026-09-30, 80.63% of stockholders' equity of USD 475 million. The creditor consequence is that growth funded by advances turns a franchisee failure into a balance-sheet loss, and because the notes are forgiven over the franchise term the cash is recovered only through fees.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Finance leadership has changed within the period covered, and the credit case rests on continuity of reporting. The 2024 annual report names Michele Allen as chief financial officer; the 2025 annual report, signed on 2026-02-19, names Kurt Albert as interim chief financial officer; an employment letter for Amit Sripathi is dated 2026-02-27 and he signed the three 2026 quarterly reports as chief financial officer; Mr. Albert's separation agreement is dated 2026-03-06. The 2026-07-23 report is signed by Nicola Rossi as chief accounting officer and the 2026-10-22 report by Christopher Androski, and the filings give no reason for the changes. The chief executive officer, Geoffrey Ballotti, is the same in the 2024 and 2025 annual reports, internal control over financial reporting is stated effective at FY2025 year-end and the auditor, Deloitte, has served since 2017. The creditor consequence is that covenant reporting and add-back policy, which carry the adjusted leverage figures, are now signed off by a new chief financial officer and chief accounting officer, with no control weakness reported.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership and takeover risk cannot be tested from the filings: no controlling holder is named, but holders of 5% or more were not supplied. The company defended an unsuccessful hostile takeover in 2024, with transaction-related costs of USD 47 million in 2024 against USD 11 million in 2023, Delaware law restricts combinations with a holder of 15% or more, and the governance documents add advance-notice rules. Shares outstanding fell 2.99% between 2026-01-31 and 2026-10-15 as buybacks outran issuance. The creditor consequence is that a leveraged takeover is the clearest discontinuity risk: a change of control is an event of default under the credit facilities, so a bid would need a refinancing or waiver of the secured debt, while whether the notes give holders a change-of-control right is not established because the indentures were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a Medium rating is the absence of any creditor-adverse structure. There is no controlling shareholder or sponsor, the sources show no dividend recapitalisation, exchange offer, priming, unrestricted-subsidiary transfer or covenant waiver, dividends of USD 127 million were 39.56% of FY2025 free cash flow, the October 2025 revolver extension and the February 2026 notes moved maturities out to 2030 and 2033, internal control is stated effective with an audit by Deloitte, and the Revo loss came from one franchisee in a base of more than six thousand. The view would improve to Low if the proxy statement showed an independent board with no holder of strategic concern, if the credit agreement's restricted-payment baskets proved tight, and if shareholder returns stayed at or below free cash flow for two consecutive years. It would worsen to High if a second large franchisee failed, if licence fees from the former parent fell materially, if a bidder or the board proposed a debt-funded transaction, or if buybacks continued above free cash flow after leverage rose.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement was not supplied, so board size, independence, committee structure, executive pay and holders of 5% or more are not established; this limits the Medium governance rating, which could move either way once the board and holders are known.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement and note indentures were not supplied, so the size of the restricted-payment baskets, the definition of change of control and the guarantor list are not established; this limits the conclusion on shareholder returns, which may be tightly capped or effectively unconstrained.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No filing after 2026-10-22 was supplied, so a further management change, financing or Revo settlement in the 27 days to the as-of date, and the reasons for the 2026 finance changes, are not established; they limit the leadership finding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Revo exposure of USD 197 million is book value before the charge, not the amount contractually owed, so the 81.22% write-off measures a loss of carrying value and not of principal; the USD 19 million of restricted cash could still change the recovery.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Licence fees from the former parent are stated only for full years, so the 2026 size of that dependency is not established and the 7.07% share is a FY2025 figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Rooms and properties are stated on the issuer's recast basis (Super 8 China excluded from 2025, Revo excluded from growth metrics), so room-growth comparisons with the 2024 annual report are not like for like and the diversification finding rests on the recast figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The selectors and registers below carry the evidence for the findings above.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The only new debt issue in the period is the February 2026 sale of USD 650 million of senior unsecured notes due 2033, with net proceeds of USD 642 million, a first call date of 2029-03-01 and semi-annual interest from 2026-09-01. The proceeds repaid revolver borrowings and term loan A, which removed the 2027 term loan maturity and left the August 2028 notes as the next large maturity, and added fixed interest of about USD 36.56 million a year. Wyndham also assumed USD 15 million of mortgages on the two European hotels it took by enforcing collateral against Revo in the first quarter of 2026.

fields.value: Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium. The risk level is driven by debt-funded shareholder returns and the Revo exposure, because both are Board choices that keep leverage up and move losses onto the balance sheet, which implies slower deleveraging and a thinner buffer if fee income falls. Countervailing evidence is the absence of any sponsor, recapitalisation, exchange offer or priming, and an effective control environment. Further analysis needs the proxy statement and the credit agreement.

fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, Inc. (wh-1722684), as of 2026-11-18, under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business and financial profile, liquidity and refinancing capacity, outlook, one downside scenario and monitoring triggers, from the five filings and the three accepted module answers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit is adequate: fee income is recurring and liquidity is USD 988 million, but net leverage of 5.48x on unadjusted EBITDA and shareholder returns above free cash flow leave little room, so creditors should underwrite to the unadjusted figure and watch distributions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest support is a franchise fee stream with free cash flow of 44.59% of adjusted EBITDA and only USD 23 million of debt due within a year. The weakest point is leverage of 4.09x even after removing the Revo charges, with distributions of 151.55% of free cash flow in the nine months to 2026-09-30. The primary downside path is a 10% fall in royalty income while buybacks continue, which lifts unadjusted net leverage to 6.16x ahead of the 2028 refinancing and hedge expiries. Covenant headroom is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C4; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage depends on which EBITDA the committee accepts, and the defensible range is 4.09x to 5.48x, not the issuer's 3.59x. Net debt of USD 2,656 million is 5.48x unadjusted EBITDA of USD 485 million and 3.59x the issuer's adjusted EBITDA of USD 740 million; removing only the Revo charges of USD 164 million gives 4.09x, because the other add-backs of USD 91 million, mainly stock-based compensation and development advance note amortization, recur every year. The creditor consequence is that the headline 3.59x understates the burden, and the reported first-lien covenant ratio of 2.0x against a 5.0x maximum, which cannot be rebuilt without the credit agreement, does not offset that.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Near-term refinancing risk is low, but rate and refinancing risks cluster in 2027 and 2028. Liquidity of USD 988 million covers the USD 542 million of debt due within 24 months 1.82x, and only USD 23 million falls due within a year, with the USD 500 million notes due in August 2028 the first large maturity. Interest rate swaps of USD 475 million expire in the fourth quarter of 2027 and USD 950 million in the second and third quarters of 2028, and they hedge over 95% of the term loan B; once they lapse, each 100 bp on USD 1,500 million would cost USD 15.00 million a year, or 4.55% of last-twelve-months free cash flow. The creditor consequence is that the 2028 notes and the swap roll-off fall in the same window, so a refinancing plan and a hedging decision are due together.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is adequate, but shareholder returns, not operations, decide whether leverage falls. Free cash flow was USD 330 million over the last twelve months, 44.59% of adjusted EBITDA, while dividends and repurchases were USD 368 million, or 111.52% of free cash flow, and 122.43% in FY2025 and 151.55% in the nine months to 2026-09-30. Had the USD 100 million by which returns exceeded free cash flow in those nine months been kept, net leverage would be 0.21x lower on unadjusted EBITDA and 0.14x lower on adjusted. The creditor consequence is that the board can restore deleveraging quickly by cutting buybacks, and has not yet done so.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is recurring, but the fee base is not growing in dollars: rooms grow and royalty income does not. System rooms grew 2.57% year on year to 2026-09-30, or 3.74% excluding Revo, yet royalties and franchise fees fell 2.62% in nine months 2026 to USD 409 million from USD 420 million, because Revo fees are deferred, all net room growth came from international rooms that earned a 2.6% royalty rate in the third quarter against 4.7% in the United States, and global RevPAR is flat over the nine months. Net revenue growth of USD 17 million came from ancillary income of USD 24 million, mainly the co-branded credit card programme, and USD 9 million of management and other fees, mainly from two owned hotels, less USD 11 million of lower royalties and franchise fees and USD 5 million of lower marketing revenue. About USD 8 million of the USD 22 million rise in adjusted EBITDA is a swing in the marketing, reservation and loyalty margin from a loss of USD 1 million to a surplus of USD 7 million, which the issuer links to the absence of the 2025 franchisee conference and to timing of spend. The creditor consequence is that recent earnings growth leans on partner fees and a better marketing margin rather than on the core fee base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Franchisee credit is the main source of loss outside the debt figure. The Revo insolvency wrote off USD 160 million of USD 197 million of book value, while development advance notes of USD 383 million equal 80.63% of stockholders' equity and the issuer guarantees a share of some franchisee construction loans in an amount it does not state. A second failure of Revo's size would cut unadjusted EBITDA by USD 160 million and lift unadjusted net leverage to 8.17x, although the adjusted figure would stay at 3.59x because the charge is added back. The creditor consequence is that growth funded by advances turns franchisee failures into balance-sheet losses, and the add-back that hides them is the one a committee should test first.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the weakest dimension and the one creditors can least control. Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk Medium: no controlling holder is disclosed, so the board alone chooses returns, it added USD 400 million of repurchase capacity in September 2026, and finance leadership changed in 2026. The issuer states ratings of Ba1 from Moody's and BB+ from S&P and Fitch, which this analysis does not rely on or replace. The creditor consequence is that policy can change faster than the credit agreement protects against, and the restricted-payment baskets were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that the issuer's own leverage is moderate and the business is cash generative. Net leverage is 3.59x on adjusted EBITDA, the reported first-lien ratio is 2.0x against a 5.0x maximum, free cash flow is positive after development advances, United States RevPAR rose 6% in the third quarter of 2026, the development pipeline is a record, the first large maturity is the USD 500 million notes in August 2028 with only USD 23 million due within a year, and the buybacks that hold leverage up are discretionary. The view would improve if distributions stayed at or below free cash flow for four consecutive quarters with net debt falling below USD 2,656 million, if royalties and franchise fees rose in dollars with rooms, and if the add-backs other than Revo proved small against cash flow. It would worsen if a second large franchisee failed, if RevPAR fell in two consecutive quarters, if the reported first-lien ratio moved towards 5.0x, or if the 2028 notes and the swap expiries approached without a refinancing and hedging plan.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Unadjusted EBITDA is calculated because the issuer states none, and the covenant EBITDA is defined in an agreement that was not supplied, so the range of 4.09x to 5.48x is not a covenant measure and the 2.0x covenant ratio cannot be reconciled to it; this limits the leverage conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The floating interest rate in force is not stated, so the cost of the term loan B after the 2027 and 2028 swap expiries is shown only as a USD 15.00 million sensitivity per 100 bp and not as a forecast; this limits the refinancing conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The downside scenario assumes a 10% fall in royalties and franchise fees and no change in costs or tax; the filings give no management projections, so the scenario sizes a sensitivity and is not a forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer or sector benchmark was supplied, so the business profile is judged against the issuer's own history and the sector risks it describes; relative strength against other franchisors is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash interest paid fell in 2026 for reasons the filings do not give, so cover on cash interest is treated as flattered and net interest expense is used for the coverage conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The amount of franchisee loans the issuer guarantees is not stated, so exposure to franchisee failure beyond the development advance notes and the Revo write-off is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The selectors, registers and analysis sections below carry the evidence for the findings above.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A recurring fee stream across a widely spread franchisee base is the main strength. Agreements run 10 to 20 years, more than six thousand franchisees pay royalties, none exceeds 2% of hotels, and free cash flow of USD 330 million over the last twelve months was 44.59% of adjusted EBITDA after development advances. This supports debt service through a slow year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and the maturity ladder give time. Liquidity of USD 988 million is 1.82x the USD 542 million due within 24 months, so a fall in fee income would reach leverage long before it reached liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A small capital need keeps margins high. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 51.18% over the last twelve months and capital expenditure 3.22% of FY2025 revenue, so little of each dollar of fees is needed to maintain the system.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Discretionary distributions are a lever. Repurchases of USD 239 million over the last twelve months can be cut without touching operations, which would let net debt fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is high on unadjusted EBITDA and has not fallen. Net leverage is 5.48x, 4.09x before the Revo charges and 3.59x on the issuer's adjusted measure, up from 4.17x at the end of FY2024 on unadjusted EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns exceed free cash flow and net borrowing funds the gap. Returns were 111.52% of free cash flow over the last twelve months and 151.55% in nine months 2026, and net debt rose USD 160 million in nine months 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Franchisee credit exposure has already cost USD 160 million. Development advance notes of USD 383 million equal 80.63% of equity, the collateral recovered so far from Revo was USD 23 million of hotel net assets, and the amount of franchisee loans the issuer guarantees is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fee base is not growing in dollars. Royalties and franchise fees fell 2.62% in nine months 2026 while rooms grew 2.57%, and growth came from partner fees and two owned hotels.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Module status: Ready with Limitations. The filings carry the evidence; the credit agreement and indentures were not supplied, so covenant headroom is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Wyndham franchises 25 hotel brands, mostly in the economy, midscale and upper midscale chain scales, and earns royalties of about 5% of gross room revenue, marketing and reservation fees, loyalty income, licence fees from the former parent and partner fees under agreements of 10 to 20 years. Only 53.39% of FY2025 net revenues is profit-bearing fee income, because the marketing, reservation and loyalty stream is passed through at close to break-even. The credit link is that cash flow is visible and recurring, but it is earned on a revenue line that overstates fee income and rests on room revenue at hotels that others own.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 80; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed, so Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, Inc. is a widely held public company and the borrower. Certain wholly owned domestic subsidiaries guarantee the credit facilities, which carry first-priority liens over substantially all assets and make up USD 1,574 million, or 57.72%, of the USD 2,727 million of debt, while the notes are unsecured and their guarantors are not named in the sources. The former parent pays licence fees equal to 7.07% of FY2025 net revenues and bears two-thirds of separation liabilities, and Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk Medium. The credit link is that the unsecured notes sit behind the secured facilities and that the owner of the cash flow is the board, not a sponsor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 121; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue follows room revenue at franchised hotels, so it moves with RevPAR and room count and shows little pricing power: the global average royalty rate was 4.0% in the third quarters of both 2026 and 2025, RevPAR fell 3.44% to USD 44.12 in FY2025 and royalties and franchise fees fell 2.52% to USD 541 million, and the issuer warns that competition may force it to lower fees. Revenue is predictable under long contracts but cyclical with leisure travel, concentrated by geography (United States 77% of royalty contribution) and exposed to substitution from short-term rentals. The credit link is that fees are sticky but do not rise with costs unless RevPAR does; the United States is recovering with RevPAR up 6% in the third quarter of 2026 while international RevPAR fell 3%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The cost base is small and mostly variable or pass-through: general and administrative expense was USD 125 million in FY2025 and capital expenditure USD 46 million, and the marketing, reservation and loyalty stream nets to roughly zero, so a fall in fees drops almost fully to EBITDA. A 10% fall in royalties and franchise fees would cut adjusted EBITDA by 7.31%. The issuer has defended margin with restructuring, a 2025 plan affecting 202 employees and a 2026 plan moving functions to a shared service center, and adjusted EBITDA margin was 50.24% in FY2025 and 51.18% over the last twelve months. The credit link is that margin withstands cost inflation better than a fee shock, and part of the 2026 gain is timing of marketing spend.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-Q_2026-03-31_wh-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is low, with capital expenditure of USD 46 million in FY2025, 3.22% of revenue, and about USD 45 million planned for 2026. The larger cash call is franchisee funding: USD 105 million of development advance notes net of repayments and USD 57 million of loans in FY2025, and about USD 110 million of advances planned for 2026, so USD 162 million went to franchisees in FY2025, 50.47% of free cash flow, with the notes paid inside operating cash flow and the loans in investing activities outside it. Free cash flow was 44.71% of adjusted EBITDA in FY2025 and 44.59% over the last twelve months, and deferred revenues of USD 354 million, flat in 2026, fund part of operating cash flow at no interest. The credit link is that conversion is less than half of adjusted EBITDA once franchisee funding is counted, and it depends on the board holding back growth advances.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 82; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4; calculation C9; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is high: Wyndham competes with other franchisors for franchisees, and the issuer says competition may force lower fees or less favourable terms, which would cut royalty income directly. New entrants matter more as supply than as rival brands, because new hotels create competitors without matching demand. Substitutes are real in economy and midscale travel, where short-term rentals, serviced apartments and cruising can take occupancy and rates from franchised hotels. Buyer power sits with franchisees, who choose brands on perceived value, are spread widely and could move to rivals at renewal, and with online travel intermediaries and large language models, which can raise distribution cost and divert bookings from direct channels. Supplier power is low for an asset-light franchisor, though reliance on third-party technology adds cyber and outage risk. The credit link is that these forces act on fee rates and occupancy rather than on cost, so they threaten the top line that supports leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulatory, economic and technology factors are material and social factors are a tail. Franchise disclosure rules and state limits on terminating franchise agreements slow the issuer's exit from a weak franchisee; minimum-tax rules and trade disputes affect international earnings; slowdowns and consumer sentiment move RevPAR; interest rates matter for the term loan B once the swaps lapse; online distribution and large language models shift cost and brand visibility; and about 80 pending human-trafficking suits, with an accrual of USD 2 million and no estimated range, add reputational and legal risk. The credit link is that these factors mostly move fees and cash costs slowly, with litigation the tail.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are recurring fees under long contracts, a widely spread franchisee base, liquidity of USD 988 million and a small capital need. Weaknesses are leverage of 4.09x to 5.48x, shareholder returns above free cash flow, a fee base that is not growing in dollars and franchisee credit exposure. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the record pipeline of about 264,000 rooms, recovering United States RevPAR, partner fee growth and a switch of buybacks to debt reduction. Threats that could weaken it are a second large franchisee failure, weaker leisure demand, a shift of bookings to online intermediaries and models, and the 2027 to 2028 hedge and notes cluster.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position are strong, because Wyndham is the largest franchisor by hotel count with about 19% of United States branded rooms in its chain scales, but competitive advantage is average, because its brands sit in lower-RevPAR segments with global RevPAR of USD 44.12 in FY2025. Business diversification is average: wide by franchisee but concentrated in the United States, which gives 77% of royalty contribution, and in related-party fees. Cost and capex flexibility is strong, because capital expenditure is 3.22% of revenue and development advances and buybacks are discretionary. Margin stability is average, given a break-even pass-through stream and USD 160 million of Revo charges in FY2025. Free cash flow stability is average, since USD 330 million over the last twelve months is positive but absorbed by returns. Ability to refinance is average, with ratings stated at Ba1 and BB+ and a 2028 cluster of notes and swap expiries. Liquidity is strong at USD 988 million. Financial policy and governance is weak, because returns exceed free cash flow. The main supports are fee income and liquidity, the main constraints are leverage and policy, the trend in unadjusted leverage is flat to higher, and the missing datapoints are covenant definitions and peer comparisons.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the issuer targets 4.0% to 4.5% net room growth in 2026 excluding Revo, capital expenditure of about USD 45 million and development advances of about USD 110 million. The pipeline of about 264,000 rooms is up 4% excluding Revo, United States RevPAR is rising and partner fees are growing, while international RevPAR is falling 3% and Revo fees stay deferred. Headwinds are a fee base that is not growing in dollars, hedge expiries from the fourth quarter of 2027, the notes due in August 2028 and any further franchisee failure. Over three to five years the term loan B falls due in May 2030, the revolver in October 2030 and the 2033 notes in March 2033, and room growth near the target adds fee base, but the royalty rate has been flat near 4.0%, so earnings growth needs RevPAR or partner fees. The credit link is that deleveraging needs EBITDA growth or lower returns, and the sources show the first slowly and not yet the second.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The scenario is issuer-specific and illustrative: royalties and franchise fees (USD 541 million in FY2025) fall 10% as RevPAR weakens, with marketing pass-through unchanged and costs held. Revenue falls by USD 54.10 million, which takes last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA from USD 740 million to USD 685.90 million and unadjusted EBITDA from USD 485 million to USD 430.90 million. With net debt unchanged at USD 2,656 million, net leverage rises to 3.87x adjusted and 6.16x unadjusted, and free cash flow falls to USD 275.90 million before any tax relief, so distributions of USD 368 million would be 133.38% of it. Liquidity of USD 988 million is not threatened and the first large maturity is the notes in August 2028, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid distress; the pressure point is leverage. Management's levers are repurchases of USD 239 million over the last twelve months, development advances and the dividend of USD 129 million, which the stressed free cash flow would cover 2.14x. A second Revo-sized failure would add a non-cash charge of USD 160 million and take unadjusted leverage to 8.17x with no change in the adjusted figure. The credit link is that the downside shows first in leverage and policy, not in liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Wyndham presents an adequate business profile supported by recurring franchise fees, a widely spread franchisee base and liquidity of USD 988 million, but credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 4.09x to 5.48x and by shareholder returns above free cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow is 44.59% of adjusted EBITDA, although it is earned on a fee base that is not growing in dollars. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the notes due in August 2028, the swap expiries from the fourth quarter of 2027 and the board's willingness to cut returns. The primary downside path is a fall in royalty income while buybacks continue. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, the indentures and the proxy statement. Fundamental credit assessment completed with limitations. Top risk: leverage held up by shareholder returns.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C1; calculation C4; calculation C7

fields.value: The orchestrator selects the next module.
